changes: original_meaning 按拉丁语 vīnea 的 gloss 收为「葡萄藤」。
semantic_path 第二站 how 补泛化的确切起点（14 世纪末，Etymonline 编年）与 vinum『酒』的得名理据，替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "vine (n.) c. 1300... \"climbing or trailing woody-stemmed plant which bears the grapes from which wine is made,\" from Old French vigne, vin \"vine, vineyard\" (12c.), from Latin vinea \"vine, vineyard,\" from vinum \"wine.\""
Etymonline: "It is attested from late 14c. in reference to any plant with a long slender stem that trails or winds around."
Oxford: "from Latin vinea 'vineyard, vine', from vinum 'wine'."
vine.mechanism_sentence: vine 的老底是「酒」：拉丁语 vinea 是结葡萄、供酿酒的藤（源头 vinum 就是 wine）——14 世纪末，它才把名字借给一切细长攀爬的藤本植物。

semantic_path.how: 从一种到一类（词义扩大）：14 世纪末 vine 从专指葡萄藤，扩到一切茎干细长、攀援缠绕或匍匐蔓延的植物——词库今义『藤；藤本植物』即此。

changes: original_meaning 保留晚期拉丁语 visibilis 的 gloss「可以被看见的」。
semantic_path 第二站 how 按 Etymonline 编年（1610 年代心智可察、1950 年代公开显眼）替换套话。
mechanism_sentence 重写（原句为罗列式）。
evidence: Etymonline: "visible (adj.) mid-14c., \"perceptible to sight, capable of being seen,\" from Old French visable, visible \"perceptible\" (12c.) and directly from Latin visibilis \"that may be seen,\" from visus, past participle of videre \"to see\""
Etymonline: "By 1610s as \"that may be mentally perceived.\" By 1950s as \"publicly prominent, well-known.\""
visible.mechanism_sentence: visible 是拉丁语「能被看见的」（videre 是「看」）：14 世纪入英语管眼睛看得见，1610 年代管心里察觉得到，20 世纪又管名声上的显眼——词库的「明显的」正是这一路。

semantic_path.how: 『看得见』从眼睛走向抽象：1610 年代添『心智上能察觉、领会』义，1950 年代添『在公众场合显眼、知名』义——词库今义『明显的』即此脉络。

changes: original_meaning 与拉丁语 vīsiō 的 gloss 对齐为「看；所见之物」。
semantic_path 按英语实史的反常次序重建三站（约 1300 年异象义先行 → 15 世纪视觉/视力回位 → 1926 年远见），现行路径把视力当作一以贯之的主线，与两源编年不合。
evidence: Etymonline: "vision (n.) c. 1300, visioun, \"that which is seen,\" specifically \"something seen in the imagination or in the supernatural\" by one sleeping or waking; from Anglo-French visioun, Old French vision \"presence, sight; view, look, appearance; dream, supernatural sight\" (12c.), from Latin visionem (nominative visio) \"act of seeing, sight, thing seen,\" noun of action from past-participle stem of videre \"to see\""

Etymonline: "By early 15c. as \"a visual perception\" (of something). The meanings \"sense of sight, faculty that perceives by the eye;\" also \"act of seeing external objects\" are recorded by late 15c. In 20c. use, \"distinct, vivid mental conception of a scheme or anticipation.\" The meaning \"statesman-like foresight, political sagacity\" is attested from 1926."
Oxford: "Middle English (denoting a supernatural apparition): via Old French from Latin visio(n-), from videre 'to see'."
vision.mechanism_sentence: vision 是拉丁语「看」的名词：它入英语时先指梦中、异象里看见的东西，15 世纪才落回日常的视力，20 世纪又长出「远见、愿景」——看的尽头，是想象。

semantic_path.how: 入英语时走了岔路：约 1300 年的 visioun 先专指『想象中或超自然中所见』（梦境、异象、幻影）；15 世纪初添普通的『视觉感知』，15 世纪末才定型为词库的『视力』本义——日常义是后来居上的。
眼睛的词去管未来（比喻）：20 世纪 vision 添『对蓝图、前景的鲜明构想』义，1926 年添『政治家的远见』义——看不见的将来，也用『看』来命名。

changes: original_meaning 保留拉丁语 vītālis 的 gloss「生命的，赋予生命的」。
semantic_path 第二站 how 写明桥接义（15 世纪末『对生命不可或缺』）与泛化年代（1610 年代），替换套话。
evidence: Etymonline: "vital (adj.) late 14c., in physiology and philosophy, \"of or pertaining to the animating principle; manifesting life,\"... from Latin vitalis \"of or belonging to life,\" from vita \"life,\" related to vivere \"to live\""

Etymonline: "The sense of \"necessary or important\" is from 1610s, via the notion of \"essential to life\" (late 15c.). Figuratively, \"that which is essential to continued existence\" of anything is by 1610s."
Oxford: "The sense 'essential' dates from the early 17th cent."
vital.mechanism_sentence: vital 是拉丁语 vita「生命」的形容词：先在生理学里管「生命的」，1610 年代借「关乎性命」的分量，泛指一切极其重要的——重要性的顶点，是拿命作比。

semantic_path.how: 一级台阶的比喻：15 世纪末 vital 先有『对维持生命不可或缺』义，1610 年代脱开生理学，泛指任何事物『关乎其存续、不可或缺』的——词库今义『极其重要的』即此。
semantic_path.meaning: 极其重要的，不可或缺的
